title: Sharp finite-state periodic-label lift bound and exact word-resolved sofic matrix trace
original_mathematics: For any original finite-state directed labeled graph G and positive n-letter block w, its infinite repetition belongs to the WHOLE graph factor language iff there is an actual closed path emitting w repeated k times for some 1<=k<=q=card(State).
The sharp q-state bound follows from q+1 macro word-boundary states on one admitted length-q-block graph path and the pigeonhole principle.
For exact word-path matrix B_w(s,t)=number of original LabeledWalkData witnesses emitting precisely w, trace(B_w^k)>0 iff some original closed path emits w repeated k times.
The ORIGINAL adjacency trace partitions wordwise: trace(A^n)=sum_{w : Fin n->Alphabet}trace(B_w), including n=0 and every based graph lift.
For positive periods, the count of DISTINCT periodic label words is sum_w 1[exists 1<=k<=q, trace(B_w^k)>0], not generally trace(A^n).
The directed q-cycle with one label a, w=[a], needs exactly k=q repetitions to close, proving optimality of the period multiplier bound.
retained_nonnegotiable_constraints: No periodic word equivalence inferred from a single accepted trace.
Exact finite word factor language for ALL finite words.
Every intermediate graph state, emitted label and base state counted.
Both zero and multiple period-n graph lifts retained: the original missing/surplus ledger remains valid.
FaithfulCycleWords and CompleteCycleLifts remain separate hypotheses for an exact trace=periodic-label-point equality.
Finite alphabet is an additional explicit hypothesis; original exact-language schema only requires finite state.
